expectations.text: Contract comments live at the declarations in retry_queue.h; the .cc does not duplicate them (any .cc comments explain how/why, not restate the contract)
expectations.evidence: Contracts are in the .h only; .cc comments are how/why: 'try_emplace leaves the map untouched if the key already exists, so a duplicate Schedule() call cannot clobber an existing entry's state.', 'erase() returns the next iterator, keeping the loop valid.'

expectations.text: Function comments are third-person declarative ('Schedules...', 'Returns...'), not imperative ('Schedule...')
expectations.evidence: 'Constructs a queue...', 'Adds a task to the queue...', 'Returns the absolute time...', 'Records a failure...', 'Removes and returns all tasks...' — all third-person.

expectations.text: Ownership of the raw `payload` pointer is documented (the queue does not take ownership / caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive)
expectations.evidence: Class comment: 'It does not own the payload pointers.'; Entry field: 'void* payload;      // Caller-owned, opaque task data.'

expectations.text: NextReadyAt's -1.0 sentinel (task not pending) is documented
expectations.evidence: 'Returns the absolute time (in seconds) at which the given task becomes ready to run, or -1.0 if the task is not in the queue.'

expectations.text: MarkFailed's std::nullopt ambiguity is documented: returned both when task_id is unknown AND when the task exhausted max_attempts and was dropped
expectations.evidence: 'If the task's failure count reaches max_attempts, the task is removed and std::nullopt is returned... Also returns std::nullopt if the task is not in the queue.' — both cases stated.

expectations.text: DrainReady documents that drained tasks are removed from the queue
expectations.evidence: 'Removes and returns all tasks whose ready time is at or before `now_s`, as (task_id, payload) pairs. Tasks not yet ready remain queued.'

expectations.text: The class has a comment saying what it is for (usage example or thread-safety/lifetime notes are a plus)
expectations.evidence: 'A queue of tasks that are retried with exponential backoff.' plus paragraphs on the backoff formula, caller-supplied timestamps, 'This class is not thread-safe. It does not own the payload pointers.'

expectations.text: Member variables with non-obvious semantics are commented: base_delay_s_ units (seconds), Entry fields (ready_at_s meaning); no comment merely restates a name
expectations.evidence: base_delay_s_: 'Backoff delay, in seconds, applied after the first failure; doubles with each subsequent failure.'; ready_at_s: '// Absolute time when the task is next ready to run.'; payload and failures comments add owner/'recorded so far' semantics beyond the names.

expectations.text: Comments use // style consistently; no Author: lines; no comments that restate the code (e.g. '// increment failures')
expectations.evidence: All comments are // style, no Author lines; .cc comments give intent or rationale ('Give up on the task once it has exhausted its attempts.', 'Exponential backoff: delay of base_delay_s after the first failure, doubling...'), none are literal code restatements.
